findings: [4] The mother is called «Панни Пшиздецкая» (Panni Pshizdetskaya); Polish panni/panna is the word for an unmarried woman, and the finished story has «пани» (pani, 'Mrs.'). Possibly a slip for «Пани». Kept as 'Panni'.
[9] The dictation «La maison написали? du prisonnier [^11]... opens with « but has no closing »; the English closes the quotation after the ellipsis.
[18] «чтобы-нибудь» (chtoby-nibud', not a word) is a slip for «что-нибудь» (chto-nibud', 'something'); translated 'something'.
[32] An empty «<sup></sup>» tag follows the [^19] marker (apparently a conversion artifact); kept as printed.

[63] The last sentence breaks off grammatically: «между бесконечными непаханными поросшими прошлогодним серебристо белым ковылем, дороге» ('between endless, unplowed, overgrown with last year's silvery-white feather grass, road'). The noun after the adjectives (perhaps 'steppes') is missing, and «дороге» ('road') is repeated. Translated as printed.
[83] Stray comma in «Альбина, продолжала» ('Albina, went on'); omitted in the English.
[84] The heading prints «ІІ» with Cyrillic/Ukrainian І letters instead of the Roman numeral II; rendered 'II'.
[92] Stray comma in «и, после, всех попыток» ('and, after, all the attempts'); translated 'and, after all the attempts'.
[96] The heading reads «(рук. 11, к гл. V)» without «№» (No.), unlike the other headings; kept as 'MS. 11'.
[98] Stray comma in «как сама с собою, называла его она» ('as she herself, to herself, called him'); the English comma happens to fall in the same place.
[105] Stray comma in «бывшим ксендзом и, приором Сироцинским» ('the former priest and, prior Sierociński'); omitted in the English.
[113] The priest's name is spelled «Сероцинского» (Serotsinskogo) here and «Сироцинский» (Sirotsinsky) elsewhere; normalized to 'Sierociński'.

[114] «слабым прерывающимся стоном голосом» ('in a weak, breaking groan voice') is garbled, perhaps for «стонами» (stonami, 'by groans'); translated 'in a weak voice broken by groans'. The Latin prayer ends with a closing » but has no opening «; the English supplies the opening mark. «secundam» is kept as printed (Vulgate: secundum).

[120] «Приорский» (Priorsky) is not otherwise known. It is perhaps a slip for «Пиотровский» (Piotrovsky), the one successful escaper named in the deleted passages of blocks 33, 34, and 36. Kept as 'Priorski'.
[126] Six men are sentenced to 7000 blows here, but [128] in the same draft says «тех пятерых» (tekh pyaterykh, 'those five'); Tolstoy's own inconsistency, translated as printed.
[129] «содатам» (sodatam) is a slip for «солдатам» (soldatam, 'to the soldiers'); translated 'to the soldiers'.
[130] The heading reads «рук. 12» (ruk. 12) without «№» (No.), unlike the other headings; translated as printed 'MS. 12'.
[156] «воскрикнул» (voskriknul) is a slip for «вскрикнул» (vskriknul, 'cried out'); translated 'cried out'.

[218] «ее отчаяние перед потерей всякой надежды спасения и страха за своего мужа было еще сильнее» (genitive «страха» (strakha, 'of fear') and singular «было» (bylo, 'was')) differs from the parallel [204] «и страх … были» (i strakh … byli, 'and fear … were'); possibly a slip, translated as printed ('and of fear for her husband was stronger still').
[228] «взглянул на ее» (vzglyanul na ee) is a slip for «на нее» (na nee, 'at her'); translated 'glanced at her'.
[232] The heading «(рук. № 9 <sub>f</sub> к гл. XII)» has a stray «<sub>f</sub>» where a comma is expected (transcription artifact); kept as printed.
[272] [^27] «вытянутыйбатальон» (vytyanutyybatal'on) lacks a space ('a battalion drawn up'); translated as two words.
[272] [^31] «по волицей милости» (po volitsey milosti) is a slip for «по велицей милости» (po velitsey milosti, 'according to great mercy'), as printed correctly in [^57]; translated 'great'.
[272] [^48] The label «Зач.:» (Zach., 'Deleted') is not italic, unlike the other labels; kept roman as printed.
[272] [^80] The label «Зачеркнуто.:» (Zacherknuto, 'Deleted') has a stray period; translated '*Deleted:*'.
